title: Branch repair advice on the verifier's failure reason
summary: A detection surface that proposes a destructive repair must branch on why verification failed, not on a boolean: an unverifiable proof is not evidence of tampering.
hint_triggers: Design rule for integrity detection: a boolean verifier (isTaskVerifiablySuperseded) maps both 'the record is forged' and 'the proof could not be read' (proof_unreadable:*) to false. Any operator-facing surface that turns that result into repair advice (restore a lock, delete a mark) must carry the failure reason and branch: an unreadable proof means fix the store and re-check, never apply the destructive repair. Companion rules: compute counts and lists from one memoized evaluation of an I/O-backed predicate so they cannot disagree; echo worker-writable fields to operators only through a strict id charset (they are an injection surface for LLM operators).
